results.reason: Issue 3 identifies automatic five-year renewals under §2.2 and the 270–240 day notice window. It calls this a narrow 30-day window and says missing it means a five-year lock-in.

Issue 1 quotes §3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates) and contrasts it with the term sheet's amber glass/beer/U.S.-Canada scope. It treats Harrowgate as contractually bound by the executed text.
Issue 5 cites Recital C and receipt of the notice on August 3, 2026. It says the objection deadline was September 2, 2026, before the September 21 amendment, so the 14% increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 2 explains that the Amendment replaces §11.2, removes recall costs from the carve-outs and limits the indemnity carve-out to §9.1(c) IP claims. It says recall and injury exposure is now subject to the six-month fees cap.

The response identifies new §14.4 and notes the unilateral free assignment right, which overrides §14.3. It never states that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor. It also does not say Harrowgate itself remains bound by the consent requirement.
The response never cites §15.2 or states that written amendments take precedence over the Supply Agreement.
Issue 2 states that the cap in §11.1 is 'the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.'
The response is a memo addressed to the Partner, with numbered issues. Each issue gives the document and section ('Where') and a 'Recommended fix'.
It proposes specific language for a narrowed §3.1, a restored §11.2, a revised §2.2 renewal clause, a revised §14.4 and other provisions.
The response concludes the increase is deemed accepted and that no contractual basis remains to contest it.
The response treats §3.1 as controlling and recommends amending it; it does not say the term sheet governs.
